seen: No measurement of this game exists; none was taken, and I saw no score of it or of any parent. Its moves were compared with Fairy-Stockfish's built-in janggi (pyffish 0.0.90, random walks asking only for legal moves), never played by this project's players.

evidence.says: the chess of Korea, popular on the Korean Peninsula; professional games; the first world janggi tournament was held in Harbin in 2009; the rules: board, pieces, the pass, no stalemate, bikjang a draw

janggi has a standing place among the server's variants; the four sanctioned arrays of horses and elephants and who chooses; every piece's move including the palace diagonals; bikjang and point counting as the server applies them

tier_note: W: recorded tournaments, professional play and a server place make W2 certain; as a national game it is W5 on the record's reading, but no player count was read today, so the range is kept. L: traditional, centuries on general knowledge; no date of origin was read today, so 3 to 4.
departure: four edge rules under unlike-search.md section 1's widening: one sanctioned array (both elephants inside), where the players choose among four; bikjang allowed and ending nothing (royal_facing allowed), where it is a draw or a count of points; two passes in a row not a draw; repetition and a long run without a capture drawn, where tournament play counts points
